summary: Documented M4-S02 (Entitlement processes for Premier/Standard plus the First Response milestone type) after it reached `tested`. Re-rendered PLAN.md/CLARIFICATIONS.md from plan.json; appended 4 decisions.md entries covering the W4 checker-policy block on missing <timeTriggers>/<successActions> and its closure at the skill (D-M4S02-01, the flywheel record, D-M4S01-01 shape), the derived minutesToComplete 720 for Standard as an UNCONFIRMED placeholder (D-M4S02-02, the holiday-seed shape), the unowned settings/Entitlement.settings-meta.xml gate item (O-M4S02-01), and the Q51 half-honoured EMEA calendar divergence (O-M4S02-02); wrote 6 workbook rows (CWB-AUT-015..018 in Section 6, CWB-OTHER-027..028 in Other Configuration); minted 3 new requirements (REQ-040 Premier's 4-business-hour promise, REQ-041 Standard's derived 720-minute promise, REQ-042 the shared MilestoneType and its D10 completion binding) as traceability Matrix rows plus their Requirement-id-derivation entries; ran check_rtm.py from the build dir (42 rows, 0 coverage gaps, 0 errors, orphans dropped from 5 to 2 — the 2 remaining belong to M4-S04, outside this step's scope, exit 0 at both build and step scope); set the step to `documented`.
confidence_rationale: Every artefact produced a workbook row with a real source_req_id and a verification cell, and all three new requirements have a traceability row (the HIGH conditions), but two things needed judgment rather than a mechanical read: the checker-policy block this step inherited was closed by a skill fix mid-build, so the decisions.md entry had to reconcile two envelopes (blocked and rebuilt) rather than transcribe one; and Standard's derived 720 has no test of any kind (machine or manual) confirming its correctness, which this pass records as an explicit gap in REQ-041's row rather than a passed assertion.
